2610.09497.title: Ream: Unfolding Mutual Awareness in Human-Agent Workspaces
2610.09497.paper_summary: As AI agents work alongside humans in shared workspaces, a mutual awareness challenge arises: agents act at speeds that outpace human monitoring, and users' evolving interests are not always expressed in chat. This challenge is especially pressing in literature review, where both parties retrieve, read, and synthesize a growing body of papers. We present Ream, a literature review workspace that supports mutual awareness through structured artifacts, bidirectional engagement tracking, and localized visualizations. Users can see each party's activity within these documents, and agents can retrieve the same history to guide their work. In studies with eighteen researchers, participants used these traces to inspect evidence, steer agents, communicate through annotations, and reflect on their research focus. Shared histories also helped agents build on earlier work. These findings inform how engagement traces within shared documents can support transparency, personalized assistance, and coordination in human-agent knowledge work.
2610.09497.paper_summary_zh: 隨著人工智慧代理與人類在共享工作空間中共同工作，出現了一個相互意識的挑戰：代理的行動速度超過了人類的監控，而用戶不斷變化的興趣並不總是在聊天中表達出來。這一挑戰在文獻回顧中尤為迫切，雙方都需要檢索、閱讀和綜合不斷增長的文獻資料。我們提出了 Ream，一個支持通過結構化文物、雙向參與追蹤和本地化可視化來促進相互意識的文獻回顧工作空間。用戶可以看到這些文檔中每一方的活動，而代理也可以檢索相同的歷史以指導他們的工作。在與十八位研究者的研究中，參與者使用這些痕跡來檢查證據、引導代理、通過註釋進行溝通，以及反思他們的研究重點。共享歷史還幫助代理在早期工作上進行擴展。這些發現為如何在共享文檔中利用參與痕跡來支持透明度、個性化協助和人類-代理知識工作的協調提供了資訊。
